tools.name: get_requirements
tools.description: What the AI-labelling laws of the given markets ask of an AI-generated image, video, audio file, 3D model or text, and what a call to POST /v1/mark must send for them: the fields required, whether the visible label is needed, and what can't be marked yet. Answers from the rules the API itself enforc

tools.name: get_integration
tools.description: How to add Kennmarq.com marking to an app's code: the package to install, a server-side example that marks each generated file before it's stored or shown, the fields to send, the API key and how to check the result. Stacks: ai-sdk (Vercel AI SDK middleware), javascript (Node.js, Next.js, Bun, Deno,

tools.name: read_doc
tools.description: A Kennmarq.com documentation page as Markdown: the API reference, the guides, the SDKs and the laws pages. The index of every page, with one line each: https://kennmarq.com/llms.txt.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_requirements · Private data: get_requirements, get_integration · Public sink: get_requirements, get_integration.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_requirements · Private data: get_requirements, get_integration · Public sink: get_requirements, get_integration

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_requirements" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
